# Independent audit: co-moving conservative contact dual and full log flux

Audited in full:

- Section 7 of `candidate 4f875cf42fc6ba0a`;
- Sections 1--7 of `candidate 1a7cfa3d1047cbae`.

Result: PASS, retaining the stated actual addable physical/parameter cone,
finite proper contact sets, exact contact-minimum cover, and uniform local shape
expansion hypotheses. The new argument does not prove those hypotheses from
arbitrary cap data, differentiate optimized parameters, or establish a Gamma
payment. I independently reran both checkers: 4,621 and 813 exact checks PASS.

## 1. Moving normals and the conservative inside choice

For H_j(t)={ (N_j+t nu_j).w>=c_j+t r_j }, the margin speed on the old cap
plane is nu_j.w-r_j. The proper-section term is therefore S_j r_j-m_j.nu_j.
On an inside supporting facet the additional loss is
[(r_j-nu_j.w)/||u_j||-v]_+; on an outside supporting facet it is the negative
of [(nu_j.w-r_j)/||u_j||-v]_+. These signs agree with the direct inward-normal
strip calculation and the previously audited all-status inverse.

Dropping the inside positive hinge gives a LOWER loss while retaining the
whole inside-fiber body loss. The result is jointly concave in the actual
body velocity, normal variation and threshold speed. Proper coarea S_j>0
keeps the inverse strictly increasing and onto. Thus a positive conservative
improvement really implies an actual improvement; the direction of the
relaxation is correct.

The singleton changing-normal budget is the derivative of the exact minimum
of sum rho_j (N_j+t nu_j).w-h-epsilon A_i(t)f_t(w), with
A_i(t)=sum rho_j Gamma_t(u_j+t u'_j). At the unique old mark this adds

    sum rho_j nu_j.Y_i
       -epsilon f_i sum rho_j grad Gamma(u_j).u'_j

to the full fixed-normal body/parameter budget. The source displacement
contributes no missing first-order term: the envelope is evaluated at its old
minimizer, and the assumed uniform expansion supplies the envelope theorem.
With finitely many old contacts the derivative is the MINIMUM of these linear
contact budgets. No selection of the same mark for every direction is made.

For every new point in an assigned current fiber, its value in the exact
contact minimum is at least that minimum. Raising the weighted thresholds by
it therefore gives a nonnegative weighted buffered cap margin at that point.
This proves the actual assigned cover even for changing normals. Whole-plane
coverage is neither required nor claimed. The remaining global-depth step uses
the explicitly assumed off-assignment gaps.

## 2. Compact selectors and one common dual

The identity -s_+=inf_(0<=tau<=1)(-tau s) gives one outside density tau on
each old supporting face. Its contributions to body loss, coarea, and full
section moment are respectively

    integral tau v dS,
    integral tau dS/||u_j||,
    integral tau w dS/||u_j||.

They must use the SAME density, as they do in the sources. For finitely many
test coordinates the image of the weak-star compact interval 0<=tau<=1 is
compact and convex. Equalized linear losses depend continuously on these
moments because every coarea has the positive lower bound S_j.

Each such tuple majorizes the conservative equalized loss. Choosing the
actual signs at its solved thresholds attains equality, so that loss is the
infimum of the compact family of linear forms. Its hypograph is convex.
The common separator is therefore legitimate; it is not a minimax swap over
the original existential inside choices.

For the entire test class, the source correctly passes through finite
subcollections. Cap weights, contact weights and weighted outside densities
have a common compact feasible container. The equations and each fixed test
inequality are weak-star closed, since each specified speed is integrable on
the compact faces. Finite-intersection compactness then supplies ONE dual for
all tests. This also preserves the free cap-normal coordinates. No closedness
of the image of the physical cone is assumed.

## 3. Shared normal controls give averaged contact centroids

Using the notation of the multicontact source, independently expand the
aggregates:

    omega_ij T_ij
      =sum_ab lambda_iab theta_ijb T_ijb
      =rho_ij sum_ab lambda_iab/B_ib
      =rho_ij kappa_i.

Their cap sums are eta_i. Normal variation nu_ij is shared across contacts,
so its coefficient is

    rho_ij [sum_a kappa_ia Y_ia-kappa_i bar w_ij]
      -rho_ij e_i (0,grad Gamma(u_ij)).

Both signs of nu_ij force zero. Therefore

    bar w_ij=sum_a kappa_ia Y_ia/kappa_i
                     -(e_i/kappa_i)(0,grad Gamma(u_ij)).

The weights in the contact barycenter are kappa_ia, not e_ia. The continuous
shift uses e_i, and its normalization by kappa_i is essential. Under the old
Gamma(u)=1 normalization, grad Gamma(u)=Sigma u. The mean base may be a real
convex combination of several integer bases. No false per-contact section
centroid assertion enters later calculations.

Inside facets have body selector one and section selector zero. Outside
facets use their same effective density in both positions. This is precisely
the identity required for the allocated Gauss--Green rule: on an inside
fiber the whole body contributes its full divergence integral and no section;
on an outside fiber the zero-volume supporting cap contributes the matching
weighted facet and section moments.

## 4. Atomic forcing and the same-separator volume martingale

If every proper group had zero weight, all dual weight would be on atomic
rows. The actual normalized summed atomic hinge has D=m_A and each atomic
cap loss at least one. Thus its weighted improvement is at least
1-beta m_A>0, contradicting that SAME separator. A proper group consequently
has positive weight, and epsilon, f_ia and the coarea factors are positive,
so Delta=sum e_ia>0.

The parameter terms have sign

    sum e_ia h(Y_ia)/L_ia >=(Delta/M) integral h/L dm.

Both affine signs give equal total mass and all full first moments. Negative
finite maxima of affine functions are available actual parameter directions
and supply the finite-source allocation tests. The resulting martingale has
source sum e_ia/L_ia delta_Yia and target (Delta/M)dm/L. Its two total L moments
are Delta, hence each positive row is L-tight. This does not identify it with
a surface transport or with a separately chosen parameter-only certificate.

Every active affine plane at a source majorizes L, so L-tightness forces
contact with all those planes rowwise. Two different continuous gradients
would restrict that row to a continuous-coordinate hyperplane in every sampled
fiber, a mixed-null set. Positive source mass and target absolute continuity
exclude that. Thus the unique source continuous gradient is obtained AFTER
the volume coupling, without an assumed differentiable PL jet.

The labeled tilted mass and full first moments then follow directly from the
actual row barycenter. Multiplying by L along an L-tight row gives the ORIGINAL
volume mass of each gradient label. These are exactly the two identities (13)
in the source; no original-volume row barycenter is inferred.

## 5. Independent force and tensor calculation

At every positive contact the old affine-minus-concave minimum yields

    U_i=sum_j rho_ij u_ij
       =epsilon f_ia[a_ia+c_ia/(N L_ia)],
    kappa_ia U_i=e_ia[a_ia+c_ia/(N L_ia)].

The latter identity is the bridge between averaged section centroids and
individual energy sources. The fiber force is

    F_z=sum_ij omega_ij S_ij(z)u_ij
        -sum_(ia:p_ia=z)e_ia a_ia
        -Delta/(NM) integral_Kz grad_X log L.

The covariance force vanishes fiberwise because the quadratic is centered at
g_z; constant terms also have zero force. Summing the cap force uses
omega_ij T_ij=kappa_i rho_ij. Its base moment uses the averaged base in Section3.
After the displayed contact identity, the remaining L-gradient terms cancel
by the labeled volume mass and first-moment identities. Thus both
sum_z F_z=0 and sum_z z tensor F_z=0 hold.

For the continuous tensor, the allocated cap-section moment is exactly

    sum_j omega_ij T_ij bar X_ij tensor u_ij
       =sum_a kappa_ia y_ia tensor U_i-e_i Sigma C_i^u,
    C_i^u=sum_j rho_ij u_ij u_ij^T.

I independently expanded the remaining divergence terms:

- The energy term is Delta Id/N-sum e_ia y_ia tensor a_ia.
- The centered quadratic term is Delta Id/2+sum_i e_i Sigma C_i^u.
- The constant term is -(N+2)Delta Id/(2N).
- The logarithmic term is -Delta/(NM) integral X tensor grad_X log L.

The raw cap-volume term cancels beta M Id because proper and atomic cap
weights together sum to one and every old cap has mass Q. The Id coefficient
is zero, the Sigma C_i^u terms cancel, and the labeled first moment cancels the
remaining source c_ia tensor term. Hence the claimed continuous tensor is zero.
There is no discarded contact covariance.

The response to the formal ordinary-centroid radial array remains
-sum_z g_z.F_z. Nonaffine centroids do not cancel it, and that array is not
asserted compatible. The sources correctly retain this limitation.

## 6. Exact affine composition and the PL warning

For velocity V_z(X)=A X+Bz+c, pulled cap planes have
u'=-A^T u, a'=-B^T u and threshold speed r=u.c. On the old cap plane their
relative margin speed is -u.V. The inward body speed is -n.V. Thus on inside
facets (r-nu.w)/||u||=v, and on outside facets (nu.w-r)/||u||=v. Every
supporting hinge, including the omitted inside hinge, is pointwise zero.

The body map has a common continuous determinant, the parameter is pulled
by exact composition, E/M is invariant, and the within-fiber covariance norm
transforms with the inverse cap normal. This proves actual normalized affine
nullity without differentiating a moving parameter crease.

A formal h=-grad L.V need not be continuous for PL L and is NOT silently
inserted into the original linear parameter cone. The exact composition is
an actual response-level statement. Independently, the force and tensor
identities above were derived only after the common volume certificate
established the needed source gradients. The argument is therefore not
circular and does not assume a nonexistent uniform parameter jet.

## 7. Retained scope

This is a conservative chosen-inside dual valid for actual finite-contact
covering constructions. It does not promote exact mixed-status response
concavity, provide a separator simultaneously for all inside branch choices,
classify arbitrary nonsmooth minimizers, or prove parameter-optimized
first-order differentiability. Those remain separate issues. Within its
explicit premises, all normalizations, allocation identities and cancellations
check without repair.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
